## Source
.design/m5/42-polaris-nsids.md — REQ-4, REQ-5, AC-3, AC-5 + Suggested-decomposition PR 3.

## Surface
- New module: `polaris-types/src/lexicon_mapping.rs`
  - `pub mod error;` — `MappingError` enum
  - One mapping pair per Polaris record type: `to_lexicon_escalation(&Escalation) -> Result<polaris_lexicons::Escalation, MappingError>` + `from_lexicon_escalation(polaris_lexicons::Escalation) -> Result<Escalation, MappingError>`. Repeat for observation + evidence-pointer.
- New error file: `polaris-types/src/lexicon_mapping/error.rs`
  - `pub enum MappingError { … }` via `thiserror`
- New dependency: `polaris-lexicons` added to `polaris-types/Cargo.toml`
  - This is **the only consumer** of `polaris-lexicons` from a workspace member in this PR. The case store / API stay unaware of the wire shape.
- New test file: `polaris-types/tests/lexicon_mapping_roundtrip.rs`
  - `proptest!` block with `1000` cases per record type
- New doc file: `lexicons/mapping-matrix.md`
  - Field-by-field table: column 1 `polaris-types` field, column 2 `polaris-lexicons` field, column 3 mapping rule ("identity" / "dropped — internal-only" / "rename" / "default-filled").

## Scope
- Mapping is **hand-written**, not derived. Justification (in design):
  - Mapping has decisions a macro cannot make (default-fill missing fields, drop internal-only fields, normalize representations).
  - Internal `polaris-types::Incident` may grow fields that have no wire counterpart; the bridge absorbs this without forcing a Lexicon revision.
- Internal-only fields (`moderator_id`, `audit_chain_hash`, etc.) are explicitly DROPPED at the to-wire boundary. Each drop is annotated `// privacy: <field> never federated` in source.

## Rust-quality notes
- `MappingError` is `thiserror`-derived. Variants must carry context for diagnostics:
  ```rust
  #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
  pub enum MappingError {
      #[error(\"field {field} out of range: {value}\")]
      FieldOutOfRange { field: &'static str, value: String },
      #[error(\"unsupported variant for discriminator {discriminator}\")]
      UnsupportedVariant { discriminator: &'static str },
      #[error(\"missing required field {field}\")]
      MissingRequired { field: &'static str },
  }
  ```
  No `#[from]` on `serde_json::Error` — structured > free-form for mapping diagnostics.
- proptest strategy: implement `Arbitrary` for the in-both-representations subset only. Out-of-subset fields are populated with sentinel values that the property test explicitly ignores. Document this carve-out in `lexicon_mapping_roundtrip.rs` at the top of the proptest block.
- Avoid `clone()` on the wire types — proto-blue codegen output supports `Cow<'a, str>` for string fields; the mapping should borrow where possible (per rust-quality §6).
- Add a `#[must_use]` to every public mapping function so a forgotten `?` surfaces at compile time.
- Per rust-quality §8: doc-comment every public mapping function with `# Errors` (list every `MappingError` variant it returns) and `# Examples` (one round-trip example).

## External references
- `thiserror` derive: https://docs.rs/thiserror/2.0/thiserror/derive.Error.html
- `proptest` book: https://proptest-rs.github.io/proptest/proptest/
- `proptest::Arbitrary` impl pattern: https://proptest-rs.github.io/proptest/proptest/proptest-derive.html
- `polaris-types` current state: `/home/doll/Polaris/polaris-types/src/lib.rs` — internal types are plain serde structs with no Lexicon deps.

## Acceptance (AC-3 + AC-5)
- [ ] AC-3: `cargo test -p polaris-types --test lexicon_mapping_roundtrip` passes; the proptest block runs 1000 cases per record type and asserts round-trip identity over the documented subset.
- [ ] AC-5: At least one valid Lexicon JSON document per Polaris record type round-trips through `serde_json::from_str → from_lexicon_*` without error. Fixture files under `polaris-types/tests/fixtures/lexicons/`.
